films.name: treasury_plan
films.alt: acme-treasury forecasts the closing balance of ACME's account for eight business days against a floor of 10,000.00. The forecast is under the floor on Monday the 12th, at -16,450.00, in red: an invoice is due a day before a customer's money arrives. Its payment schedule holds that invoice, INV-E for 61,450.00, until Tuesday the 13th by setting a payment block in mock-sap, and the line is drawn again without the dip. All eight of mock-bank's statements then close where the plan said, none under the floor and the lowest at 26,050.00. On the 13th the block is lifted and the invoice is paid, one day late. The payments were made by mock-acme's payment run, and the capture script set up the invoices, paid in the customer's money on the 13th and moved both clocks.
films.caption: an overdraft forecast, and one invoice held a day to avoid it

films.name: treasury_week
films.alt: acme-treasury forecasts the closing balance of ACME's account for eight business days, from what mock-sap says is owed and what mock-bank says it holds, and draws it as a line. Monday's statement from the bank closes 9,300.00 away from the line, in red: the forecast expected to pay an invoice, and the bank refused the payment because the supplier's account is closed, which SAP did not know. Tuesday's forecast replaces the line and lists that invoice as left out, with the bank's reason. The other seven statements close where the forecast then said, one of them at -16,450.00. The payments were made by mock-acme's payment run, and the capture script set up the invoices and moved both clocks.
films.caption: a cash forecast, held to the bank's statements
